name: Zero Coefficient Ratio Is Not Preserved by Cyclic Section Gluing
statement: There are two 25-concept ample classes $A$ and $B$, each downward closed in one private coordinate and gated in their 33-concept ample common-section union $X$, such that $\tau(A)=\tau(B)=0$ but $\tau(X)=1$. Each piece supports a zero-entropy local distribution with nonzero section imbalance, and the two imbalances are opposite.
proof: Explicit term-dominance witnesses with private-row parameters $(3,1,4,2)$ and $(1,3,4,2)$ prove the two zero values. Four deterministic comparisons in each piece give opposite quarter-unit circulations around a section four-cycle; after assigning half the global mass to each piece they form a zero-entropy balance for every outer favorable distribution, so entropy composition gives $\tau(X)\geq1$. All-one coefficients with control magnitudes one, present outside magnitudes $\varepsilon$, and absent magnitudes $2+5\varepsilon$ give ratio at most $1+5\varepsilon$, proving $\tau(X)\leq1$.
comments: The scalar values of the pieces do not determine the value of their union; the shared cycle imbalance is essential.
